# Pandamonium v1.0.54

This release makes the agent's built-in catalog fully retrievable, adds agent-side extension capability inspection with on-demand mounting, and ships the staged static scan plus the GitHub intake UI for extension onboarding.

## MAD-911 — Extensions: capability inventory, lazy-mount, and scan contracts

### Problem

The extension work in this release builds on versioned contracts, and this comparison range references them directly: how installed capabilities are inventoried without implying they are live, how a turn-scoped mount injects schemas, and how a static scan stays bounded, redacted, and non-executing.

### Implementation

The v1.0.52 contracts remain the basis used by this release's agent mount (MAD-913) and staged scan (MAD-914): `specs/extension-capability-inventory-contract.md` plus the strict inventory/scan JSON schemas and the pure helpers in `src/extension_capability_inventory.py`. No contract behavior changed in this range; the scan pipeline consumes the same schema and validator.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Recorded here so the release comparison shows that MAD-913 and MAD-914 implement the shipped contracts rather than new ad-hoc shapes.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_capability_inventory_contract.py` remains green, covering the schemas, revision and digest binding, fail-closed staleness and tamper rules, sanitized advisory projection, per-turn mount resolution, and scan bounds and redaction.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Contract-only: no dependency, registry, adapter, route, or runtime behavior change.

### References

- [Linear MAD-911](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-911/extensions-define-the-capability-inventory-lazy-mount-and-scan)
- [Contracts PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/122)

## MAD-913 — Extensions: agent capability query and on-demand tool mount

### Problem

The agent could not answer "what capabilities does plugin X have?" without activating the extension, and had no way to mount a single extension capability for one turn without flooding its base tool payload.

### Implementation

Adds the agent-facing extension capability tool with bounded `list` and `inspect <extension_id>` actions (names, kinds, permission modes, activation state, and how to enable) reading the persisted inventory without enabling the extension, plus `mount` for named capabilities for the current turn. Mounted schemas inject lazily through the same path as the built-in catalog mounts, respecting `cap_tool_schemas`, the tool-catalog budget, and `_relevant_tools` pruning; execution goes through the existing extension executor and authority gate, so no second authority layer exists. Stale, tampered, disabled-without-approval, and unknown capability names fail closed, and the extension gateway prompt section stays compact.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. The agent can explain a disabled plugin's capabilities and use one on demand, while the base tool payload is unchanged until something is mounted.

### Verification

Focused contract and execution tests cover list, inspect, mount, execute, and teardown, first-load payload parity when nothing is mounted, and fail-closed behavior for stale, tampered, disabled, and unknown capabilities.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency. Mounts last for one turn and never bypass the extension authority path; only sanitized names and counts are returned unless a capability is actually mounted.

### References

- [Linear MAD-913](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-913/extensions-add-agent-capability-query-and-on-demand-tool-mount)
- [Capability mount PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/137)

## MAD-914 — Extensions: staged static scan and manifest-draft pipeline

### Problem

Installing a repository extension required hand inspection: no staged preview produced a capability and entrypoint inventory, a risk report, or a draft manifest before install, and nothing enforced bounded, non-executing analysis.

### Implementation

Adds a persisted scan job with `fetch → classify → extract → audit → report` stages and percent/phase progress suitable for the updater-style UI. Classification covers skill bundles, MCP configs, Python console scripts, Node bins and scripts, Dockerfile entrypoints, and OpenAPI specs; extraction emits candidate capabilities and endpoints with bounded, sanitized evidence paths; the audit inventories dependencies and licenses and flags secret-like strings and dangerous patterns (curl-pipe-shell, eval/exec, postinstall scripts, privileged or network binds, binary blobs, oversized files) under hard time and size bounds. Output is a draft `jarvis-extension.json` manifest validated by the existing strict validator plus a risk summary and capability-inventory seed. The pipeline never builds, installs, or runs repository code, and never reaches the network beyond the pinned fetch; artifacts are revision-bound and digest-addressed.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change in this slice; the stage and progress shape feeds the MAD-915 intake UI and the existing source-preview and authority flow.

### Verification

Focused tests cover each classifier and extractor, bound violations, fail-closed malformed/oversized/unavailable repositories, idempotent re-scan of an unchanged revision, draft-manifest validation, and the no-execution guarantee.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency. The MCP probe remains the single explicit runtime verification stage; findings never persist or return secret values.

### References

- [Linear MAD-914](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-914/extensions-add-staged-static-scan-and-manifest-draft-pipeline)
- [Static scan PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/145)

## MAD-915 — Extensions: add GitHub intake and scan progress UI

### Problem

The static scan had no operator surface: there was no place to paste a repository link, watch staged progress, or review extracted capabilities and risks before approving an install.

### Implementation

Adds a GitHub intake flow to the Plugins/marketplace surface: URL plus optional ref, start scan, and a progress panel reusing the updater pattern (phase list, percent, current detail, explicit terminal and failure states with safe retry). The review step shows the capability and endpoint list, permissions, dependency and license summary, structured findings with severity, and the draft manifest preview with a clear no-execution note. Approving installs through the existing `POST /api/extensions/plans/source` preview, authority decision, and plan execution, and the sidebar refreshes via the existing extensions-changed event. Only operator-provided public repository URLs are accepted, and findings mask evidence so no secret values, absolute paths, or private endpoints reach the DOM or payloads.

### Product value and UI visibility

The Plugins surface gains a guided intake wizard with updater-style progress and a review step; it is responsive on desktop and mobile and keeps the marketplace's keyboard accessibility. When no scan is running, the surface is unchanged.

### Verification

Browser tests cover the happy path (paste, progress, review, approve, sidebar refresh), scan failure and retry, finding severity rendering, evidence masking in DOM and payloads, and mobile layout, with API routes stubbed through the shared shell harness.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency and no change to the install lifecycle; scans require a public repository URL and reuse the pinned-fetch static pipeline.

### References

- [Linear MAD-915](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-915/extensions-add-github-intake-and-scan-progress-ui)
- [Intake UI PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/147)

## MAD-919 — Agent: page and filter the built-in catalog listing

### Problem

On v1.0.52 the built-in catalog mounted correctly, but `manage_settings action=list_tools` returned a ~15.3k-char structured payload that the tool-result formatter caps at 8,000 chars — the model saw a mid-JSON dump cut off at roughly 42 of 81 tools and could only report partial category counts.

### Implementation

`list_tools` now returns one bounded page: `offset` (default 0), `limit` (default 20, max 50), optional `category` and `search`, plus `total`, `count`, `next_offset`, `enabled_count`, and `categories`. Entries are compacted to id, category, a ~100-char description, and enabled state, so every page stays under the model-visible budget; a pure `catalog_page()` helper backs the action and the tests, and the response text states the shown range, the total, and how to continue.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. "How many tools do you have?" is answered instantly from `total`, and the full catalog is enumerable across pages without truncation.

### Verification

`tests/test_tool_catalog_paging.py` enforces the per-page 8,000-char budget, complete and duplicate-free paging, category and search filters, and count-without-paging; 268 focused catalog and agent regression tests pass.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency. `load_tools` behavior is unchanged, disabled tools remain reported, and intent clamps still apply.

### References

- [Linear MAD-919](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-919/agent-page-and-filter-the-built-in-catalog-listing-so-list-tools-never)
- [Catalog paging PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/141)
